mfrmr Compatibility Layer Map

Source: R/help_compatibility_layer.R
mfrmr_compatibility_layer.Rd

Guide to the legacy-compatible wrappers and text/file exports in mfrmr. Use this page when you need continuity with older compatibility-oriented workflows, fixed-width reports, or graph/score file style outputs.

This compatibility layer currently applies mainly to diagnostics-based RSM / PCM workflows. Supported GPCM fits also provide graph and package-native scorefile exports through facets_output_file_bundle(), with explicit score-side limitations. Check each helper's model scope. Treat this layer as a presentation/contract surface, not as a claim of FACETS or ConQuest numerical equivalence.

SPSS is treated differently from FACETS and ConQuest: mfrmr currently supports table/data-frame/CSV handoff for SPSS-oriented reporting workflows, but it does not generate SPSS syntax, write native SPSS system files, execute SPSS estimators, or claim SPSS numerical equivalence.

When to use this layer

  • You are reproducing an older workflow that expects one-shot wrappers.

  • You need fixed-width text blocks for console, logs, or archival handoff.

  • You need graphfile or scorefile style outputs for downstream legacy tools.

  • You are checking column coverage and metric consistency against a FACETS-style output contract.

When not to use this layer

  • For standard estimation, use fit_mfrm() plus diagnose_mfrm().

  • For report bundles, use mfrmr_reports_and_tables.

  • For manuscript text, use build_apa_outputs() and reporting_checklist().

  • For visual follow-up, use mfrmr_visual_diagnostics.

Compatibility map

facets_positioning_guide()

User-facing wording for the package's relationship to FACETS. Use before describing compatibility outputs in a report or migration note.

run_mfrm_facets()

One-shot legacy-compatible wrapper that fits, diagnoses, and returns key tables in one object.

mfrmRFacets()

Alias for run_mfrm_facets() kept for continuity.

build_fixed_reports()

Fixed-width interaction and pairwise text blocks. Best when a text-only compatibility artifact is required.

facets_output_file_bundle()

Graphfile/scorefile style CSV and fixed-width exports for legacy pipelines.

write_mfrm_residual_file()

Package-native observation-level residual CSV/TSV export for reviewer, spreadsheet, or external QC handoff.

write_mfrm_subset_file()

Package-native connected-subset summary and node-membership CSV/TSV export for linking review handoff.

facets_output_contract_review()

Column and metric review against the FACETS-style output-contract specification. Use only when an explicit output-contract review is part of the task; it checks the package output contract and does not imply external FACETS equivalence.

Preferred replacements

  • Instead of run_mfrm_facets(), prefer: fit_mfrm() -> diagnose_mfrm() -> reporting_checklist().

  • Instead of build_fixed_reports(), prefer: bias_interaction_report() -> build_apa_outputs().

  • Instead of facets_output_file_bundle(), prefer: category_curves_report() or category_structure_report() plus export_mfrm_bundle().

  • For residual or subset handoff, prefer write_mfrm_residual_file() and write_mfrm_subset_file() over reusing graph/score compatibility exports.

  • Instead of facets_output_contract_review() for routine QA, prefer: reference_case_review() for package-native completeness review or reference_case_benchmark() for packaged benchmark cases.

Multiple-imputation review and intervals in 0.2.4

Re-run pool_mfrm_imputed() on saved, valid fit_mfrm_imputed() analyses to obtain IntervalReason and saved inference notes, then recreate plots and exports. No new imputations or fitted analyses are needed for the interval arithmetic update. Numerically unresolved intervals keep their estimates and variances with missing bounds. Older saved tables lack this audit.

review_mfrm_imputations() now rejects numeric IDs that collapse to the same text and detects changes to observed numeric predictors without text rounding. Numeric predictors must stay numeric in completed data; integer and double storage are interchangeable. Pooling rechecks the original roster and saved assignment/support review. Correct changed inputs from their original evidence and recreate affected reviews/analyses; do not overwrite original values to make an invalid completion pass.

Expected agreement and accuracy identifiers in 0.2.4

Regenerate diagnose_mfrm() from the saved fit, then recreate interrater_agreement_table() and derived reports or exports. Calibration refitting is unnecessary. Observed agreement remains available when primary fitted estimates are unavailable; model-expected agreement is withheld instead of using finite optimizer proxies. New ExpectedReason fields distinguish these cases from repeated ratings and unavailable probabilities. Older diagnostics do not contain this audit; reports identify its absence and request regeneration before interpreting model expectations. The MML baseline remains a conditional EAP plug-in quantity, not posterior-integrated agreement.

fit_rater_accuracy() rejects numeric identifiers whose conversion to text would merge distinct values. Replace them with unambiguous character IDs from the original data before fitting; already rounded text cannot recover the original identities. Previously affected accuracy fits need to be regenerated from corrected input.

Halo-network inference in 0.2.4

Recreate rater_halo_network_analysis() results from the original fit and matching saved diagnostics before summary, plotting or export. No model refit is needed. Older results lack the Person-level availability audit and are rejected by summary and plot methods. Correlations remain available when Persons repeat across shared contexts, but ordinary independent-pair p-values are withheld with counts and reasons. Context definitions omitting "Person" also provide descriptive correlations only. Use alpha = 1 for an explicitly descriptive graph without a p-value filter; this does not supply missing inference. Regenerate derived plots and CSV files.

Simulation, assignment review and GPCM guidance in 0.2.4

These old public function names have been replaced, rather than retained as callable aliases. Their help aliases lead to the new topics.

Former callCurrent callWhat it does
evaluate_mfrm_recovery(...)simulate_mfrm_recovery(...)Generate data repeatedly, refit, and summarize parameter recovery.
build_peer_review_design_review(x)review_peer_design(x)Read existing peer-assessment assignment metadata; no assignment generation or model fitting.
gpcm_score_side_contract(status)gpcm_capability_matrix(status, view = "scores")Read score availability, limitations and alternatives.
gpcm_runtime_guard_coverage()gpcm_capability_matrix(view = "unavailable")Read blocked/deferred workflows and alternatives.

assess_mfrm_recovery(x, ...) keeps its name: it applies review thresholds to an existing simulation result without generating data or refitting. Unused arguments are now rejected, so misspelled options cannot silently leave a requested threshold unapplied. Review thresholds are aids to interpretation, not universal validity criteria.

The simulation and peer-design replacements retain their argument lists, defaults, numerical calculations and result classes. Existing RDS objects still work with summary(), supported plot() methods and reporting helpers; no re-estimation or class relabelling is needed for these naming changes. Each GPCM view retains its previous columns and status meanings. The default workflow view is unchanged apart from updated route names. Existing scorefile bundles keep the component gpcm_score_side_contract and its CSV filename for saved-output compatibility; this field name is not a callable function.

CSV export name in 0.2.4

Replace export_mfrm(fit, ...) with export_mfrm_tables() using the same arguments. The old function is no longer exported; its help alias opens the replacement's help. CSV filenames, numeric values and the returned file table are unchanged by the rename. Enriched facet CSVs additionally retain diagnostic availability, SE/inference qualifications and reasons, and follow the source facet-table order. Existing fits do not need re-estimation; regenerate older CSVs from the fit and matching diagnostics to include these fields. Do not infer approval from their absence in an older CSV.

export_mfrm_results() and export_mfrm_bundle() retain their names because they serve different tasks: the former archives an existing results object and reloads its RDS, while the latter prepares fit-level artifacts with an optional refitting recipe. Neither is an alias for the CSV-only exporter. ZIP replacement now includes only files written by the current call; older members are not carried forward. If ZIP creation fails, the prior archive is retained but is not reported as a successful current export. See mfrmr_reports_and_tables for the saving routes.

Practical migration rules

Recompute older mantel_haenszel_table() results from their original input data if large strata produced integer-overflow warnings or unavailable odds ratios/tests/intervals. Merely reopening the saved list does not repair it. The corrected calculation preserves the statistical method, matching and multiplicity settings; no MFRM fitting is involved. Regenerate CSV exports from the new result.

  • Start FACETS-facing reports with facets_positioning_guide() when readers might otherwise assume FACETS numerical reproduction.

  • Keep compatibility wrappers only where a downstream consumer truly needs the old layout or fixed-width format.

  • For new scripts, start from package-native bundles and add compatibility outputs only at the export boundary.

  • Treat compatibility outputs as presentation contracts, not as the primary analysis objects.

  • Use compatibility_alias_table() when you need to check which aliases are still retained and which package-native names should be used in new code.

  • Use reporting_checklist(fit)$software_scope to review the current FACETS, ConQuest, and SPSS relationship wording for a fitted analysis.

G/D-study entry points in 0.2.4

Use mfrm_g_study() for one or several observed score columns and mfrm_d_study() for the resulting assessment plans. The former public names are replaced as follows:

Former callCurrent call
mfrm_multivariate_gstudy(data, scores, ...)mfrm_g_study(data, scores, ...)
mfrm_multivariate_d_study(g, plans, weights)mfrm_d_study(g, plans, weights = weights)
mfrm_d_study(main_effects, plans, residual_scaling = ...)Same call; the main-effects approximation is retained.

The two former long names are no longer exported functions; their help aliases lead to the replacement pages. Constructor arguments, ANOVA/MINQUE defaults, result classes and stored estimates are preserved. Existing G/D RDS files can be reloaded and passed to mfrm_d_study(), summary(), plot() and the same supported interval methods without re-estimation. This naming change alone does not require recreating a saved analysis.

Both D-study routes accept facet labels or n_<facet> count columns, for example n_Rater and n_Task. Existing task/rater Raters/Tasks names remain accepted for results that use them. Supply one count per facet; duplicate aliases, extra columns and ambiguous matches are errors. Returned count columns retain the source result's convention so plot selections and saved interval identities stay unchanged. A nested child count still means children per parent, not the total number of children.

summary(d) returns the coefficient data frame for either route. For a main-effects D-study this replaces generic per-column descriptive summaries; use summary(as.data.frame(d)) if those summaries were intended. Unsupported arguments to an already estimated G-study are now rejected instead of ignored. Composite weights require the score-component route; residual_scaling belongs only to the main-effects approximation. Supplying a fitted MFRM still estimates a separate observed-score main-effects G-study first. Dispatch does not change an estimator or add interval support to that approximation.

Standard R extraction in 0.2.4

Native fits now have documented coefficient, covariance, likelihood and count methods. Previously, coef(fit) could fall through to NULL, and ordinary MML fits lacked vcov() and logLik(). Use coef(fit) for free coordinates matched to vcov(fit), or coef(fit, type = "locations") for labelled saved facet locations. These vectors answer different questions; do not combine a component vector with the free-coordinate covariance without its constraint map. Existing summary(fit) tables remain the route to estimates with status and interpretation. CML's existing covariance and likelihood values retain their meanings; the new coef() uses the same conditional coordinates.

confint(fit) now returns pointwise intervals for those default coefficients for supported native MML/CML fits. Use names or integer positions in parm to select coefficients. The matrix carries estimates, SEs, availability reasons and checks in its attributes; comparison-only CML retains missing rows for unidentified targets. JML structural-truth intervals remain unsupported. CML uses saved conditional information; MML applies the same covariance qualification as vcov().

Breaking change for GPCM: replace confint(fit, ...) with confint(fit, parm = "slopes", ...) when requesting slope intervals, ratios/differences, standardization, sandwich or profile inference, or preparing slope plots/report attachments. The default coefficient matrix uses free log-slope coordinates and is a different target. Supplying slope options without parm = "slopes" is rejected. Existing saved slope-interval objects remain reusable; no refit or recomputation is needed merely to change the call syntax. Bootstrap-result and extended-model methods retain their own defaults. See confint.mfrm_fit().

nobs(fit) counts Persons for MML/CML and retained ratings for JML. Use nobs(fit, type = "ratings") for a response-row count in every method. logLik(fit) retains the likelihood basis and information-criterion reason; unqualified ordinary results give df = NA, so AIC/BIC remain unavailable. Multiple-model AIC()/BIC() calls now direct users to compare_mfrm() rather than allowing conditional and marginal likelihoods to be mixed. Current native saved fits can use these methods after reloading; source objects are not rewritten. Legacy likelihood metadata, corrected/penalized objectives and unsupported model classes require their documented summaries.

Native ordinary fits also support fitted rating and residual methods. Previously fitted(fit) and residuals(fit) could silently return NULL. They now return retained-row vectors; fitted(fit, type = "prob") returns category probabilities. predict(fit) has the same source-rating target. predict(fit, newdata = ...) is explicitly unsupported; retain predict_mfrm_units() or score_mfrm_calibration() for ability scoring from supplied responses. These targets must not be interchanged.

MML probabilities are evaluated at the saved EAP, not averaged over its posterior distribution. JML uses primary estimates, including limiting probabilities for extreme Persons. Zero-variance Pearson residuals are missing with a reason. Legacy diagnose_mfrm() helpers retain finite JML optimizer proxies and their small-variance cutoff, so values can differ at these limits. Diagnostic observation/score/residual tables now include PrimaryPersonMeasure, PersonMeasureBasis, ConditionalVariance, PearsonAvailable and row-specific reasons. Overall/element mean squares are unavailable when any contributing standardized residual, variance or weight is unavailable; FitAvailableRows, FitUnavailableRows and FitReason expose that coverage. Older diagnostics could effectively count missing residuals as zero misfit. Regenerate them and their exports from the saved fit, without refitting. MML response calculations now match Persons by identifier even when the saved Person table is reordered.

Read the diagnostics, settings, score_map and source_readiness attributes; values alone do not establish fit or inference readiness. Outputs align with fit$prep$data, not an unfiltered input table. Existing saved fits can be reused without refitting. When old objects lack omitted-row identities, their original InputRow positions remain NA; retained-row order is still available. CML and comparison-only results now explicitly refuse this unsupported Person plug-in target instead of letting fitted()/residuals() fall through to NULL.

Input normalization corrections in 0.2.4

The shared preparation used by fit_mfrm(), describe_mfrm_data() and anchor review now rounds scores within 1e-6 of an integer to that integer. Earlier preparation accepted that tolerance but then truncated toward zero: for example, 1.9999999 could become category 1 rather than category 2. The new score_roundoff_normalized preparation note records affected retained rows. Genuine fractional responses still require explicit recoding. Corrected JML and two-family GPCM retain their stricter exact-integer input checks; explicitly normalize roundoff before using those specialized fits. Numeric observation weights no longer pass through character formatting; their supplied precision is retained. Out-of-range integer category codes, nonrepresentable category spans and overflowing retained-weight totals are refused before likelihood construction.

Grouped and rowwise tibbles now behave like their ungrouped versions. Only selected model columns enter preparation; grouping on an unused column does not add that column to the design or remove rows for its missing values. This is one combined analysis, not a separate model for each dplyr group.

Facets named Person, Score, Weight, score_k, theta, steps, interactions, log_slopes, beta or log_sigma2 are now refused before they can collide with internal data or parameter blocks. Rename the facet and update the facets argument and any step/slope-owner or anchor references to it. This restriction does not prevent using those names for their intended person, score or observation-weight roles. For example, rename a facet column steps to Stage and replace facets = c("Rater", "steps") with facets = c("Rater", "Stage"), also updating any step_facet, slope_facet, interaction and anchor references. Similar names such as log_sigma2_group remain supported. Internal parameter lookup now matches names exactly, preventing those columns from being mistaken for population or slope parameters when those blocks are absent. Older fits using such prefixes should be refitted with the same settings if their calculation entered an affected path, including adaptive MML, where the former partial matching could alter the gradient.

If an older fit was affected by category truncation or a column collision, refit from the original corrected data and regenerate its derived results. Editing prep$data, score_map, parameter names or identity metadata in a saved fit cannot repair estimates computed from a different response coding. Exact integer inputs with ordinary facet names keep their existing preparation behavior.

Likelihood and convergence corrections in 0.2.4

JML/MML category and posterior normalization now preserve probabilities and log likelihoods when finite log weights share a large offset. Earlier paths could lose the normalizing term through cancellation, even though no exponential overflow occurred. Fits whose estimates or numerical checks entered this regime need refitting with the same data/model and a new numerical review. Saved estimates and derived outputs do not update when the package is updated; do not edit their stored likelihood or readiness flags.

Optimizer code zero no longer gives a numerical pass when the terminal gradient is absent, incomplete or contains NA/NaN/Inf. In that case the result reports code_zero_unavailable_gradient and remains review-only. Older saved fits with missing or nonfinite gradient diagnostics must not be treated as qualified merely because their stored convergence code is zero. Refitting under the current checks is required before relying on their numerical-readiness claim. A finite recorded norm alone cannot establish that an older full gradient was valid, because earlier code discarded nonfinite entries when calculating that norm. These corrections do not change the response model, estimator, quadrature order or tolerance.

Optimizer polishing now rejects candidates with a worse likelihood beyond floating-point rounding error, even if their terminal gradient is smaller. Earlier acceptance used a relative allowance that grew with the objective magnitude. If a saved fit selected such a worse polishing stage, refit with the original data/model/settings and regenerate dependent inference; editing its saved optimizer history does not repair the retained estimates. MML solution checks now return an ineligible result with a reason when likelihood, gradient-norm or information summaries are missing or invalid.

Two-family GPCM/GMFRM EM also uses the stable Person-posterior normalization: large common log likelihoods no longer erase quadrature weights or inflate expected response counts. Its log-slope derivatives and the ordinary GPCM JML/MML derivatives avoid cancellation at large, nearly tied category logits. Refit calibrations affected by these numerical defects with their original data and model settings before reusing inference.

GPCM profile intervals now require positive nuisance curvature at both integration orders, in addition to their existing optimizer, gradient and start-agreement checks. A shared stationary point need not maximize the constrained likelihood. Recompute saved profile intervals with confint(fit, parm = "slopes", method = "profile", slope = ...) to apply this additional check; stored intervals do not update automatically. The source calibration can be reused if it remains eligible and was unaffected by the fitting corrections above. An unresolved curvature check leaves missing bounds and a reason; it does not prove that an interval does not exist. Passing these local checks does not establish a global optimum or sampling coverage.

Updating saved ability scores in 0.2.4

New-Person and portable-calibration scoring now remove common log-likelihood offsets before applying quadrature weights. This prevents distorted EAPs and posterior SDs when finite likelihood terms are very large in magnitude. Continuous posterior intervals and cut-score probabilities likewise center the likelihood before adding the prior density; otherwise even an ability-independent likelihood could change a normal-prior interval.

Recompute affected scores with predict_mfrm_units() or score_mfrm_calibration(), preserving the input rows, calibration, scoring prior, weights, interval level and any cut scores. Regenerate plausible values with the original seed and settings using sample_mfrm_plausible_values(). Saved summaries and draws do not update automatically. A scoring-only correction can reuse an eligible unchanged calibration; if its fitted likelihood or convergence checks were affected by the corrections above, refit and review that calibration first. Intervals remain conditional on the point calibration and supplied prior; this correction does not establish frequentist coverage or include calibration uncertainty.

The same likelihood-centering correction applies to ordinary source-Person, testlet and shared-rater continuous scoring. Recompute source scores with score_mfrm_persons(). For a supplied roster, use predict.mfrm_testlet() or score_mfrm_random_rater() with the original complete roster and settings. Recompute affected response diagnostics with mfrm_response_diagnostics(). Testlet nested integration and the shared-rater likelihood also correct cancellation at large finite category ties; calibrations affected during estimation require refitting and renewed numerical checks before reuse. Testlet derivatives now handle a single latent point without dropping a matrix dimension. None of these corrections certify the separate shared-rater Laplace approximation or calibration-adjusted interval coverage.

Updating saved diagnostics in 0.2.4

When a report, plot, bias screen or export accepts both fit and diagnostics, the diagnostic object must describe that same fitted analysis. Matching person/facet labels or location estimates alone is insufficient: thresholds, population specification, integration settings and retained observations must also agree. A mismatched pair now raises an error instead of combining results or silently substituting newly computed diagnostics.

Corrected diagnostic and bias bundles carry calculation_version = 2. Earlier bundles must be recreated from the saved fit, including estimate_bias() and derived reports. Corrections affect PTMEA, ZSTD, displacement, chi-square df, PCM fair scores, bias expectations and summary tests, and unexpected-response screening. The diagnostic default is now fit_df_method = "facets". Fit-measure tables and ZSTD fit-pathway plots use this default too; request the explicit engine option for historical df. whexact = TRUE now means FACETS WHEXACT=NO; use "legacy_linear" for its former calculation. Reproducing the former engine convention also requires fit_df_method = "engine". The former unexpected-response rule is explicit abs_z_min = 2, rule = "either". Pairwise reports now use modified Rasch-Welch df rounded down by default; df_method = "classical" retains the former continuous reference. Recreate those reports to obtain CalculationVersion = 3. Recompute rather than inserting a version field into an old object. These are diagnostic changes and do not require a main calibration refit.

Older native diagnostics that lack a saved calibration identity are also refused when paired with a fit. For native models supported by diagnose_mfrm(), regenerate diagnostics from the original saved fit; the model does not need to be refitted. Reuse the diagnostic options from your original analysis, such as diagnostic_mode and residual_pca. For example, if the original options were "legacy" and "none":


fit <- readRDS("fit.rds")
diagnostics <- diagnose_mfrm(
  fit, diagnostic_mode = "legacy", residual_pca = "none"
)
saveRDS(diagnostics, "diagnostics-0.2.4.rds")
report <- facet_quality_dashboard(fit, diagnostics = diagnostics)

Function signatures and result-table columns are unchanged by this identity check. Helpers that explicitly accept diagnostics alone, such as fit_measures_table(diagnostics), still support that input; it does not establish a match to another fit. Imported diagnostics must be the bundle stored in the matching imported fit. These checks do not expand the model families supported by ordinary diagnostics; for example, native CML retains its separate interval/reporting workflow in mfrm_facet_intervals().

Updating saved shrinkage results in 0.2.4

Reapply apply_empirical_bayes_shrinkage() to the saved fit using the original prior settings, then regenerate plots and exports. No MFRM refit is needed. Updated reports record CalculationVersion = 2; calculations avoid artificial zero SEs and retained weights caused by subtracting a shrinkage factor rounded to one.

shrink_person = TRUE now requires ordinary JML. For MML or other estimators, use shrink_person = FALSE: this removes any previous extra Person adjustment and retains the original Person estimates. MML EAP and posterior SD already describe a posterior distribution; treating them as an observation and sampling SE for another normal update is unsupported. Non-Person facet adjustment remains available within its existing scope.

Updating saved screening results in 0.2.4

Recompute detect_anchor_drift() and build_equating_chain() from saved fitted waves to apply stable offset/SE calculations and explicit unavailable states. No model refit is required. Singleton or uncomputable residual spreads now remain missing, and summaries distinguish unavailable flags from zero flagged elements. The result records fallback and actual offset contributors; chains also record unavailable cumulative sums. Earlier saved tables are not repaired by loading them. Rebuild chains before requesting offset sensitivity if the saved offsets no longer match the current arithmetic. Regenerate plots and exports: as_ggplot() now uses the selected drift, wave estimate, cumulative offset or common-element count instead of the first numeric column.

Rerun analyze_dff() with method = "refit" from the saved baseline fit and original data to repair earlier subgroup results. This reruns subgroup estimation: failed/skipped groups no longer borrow baseline estimates, absent target levels remain visible, and sparsity/precision screens use retained target-cell counts and shared-Person checks. Current summary, report and plotting methods reject earlier refit objects; do not add the version field by hand. Regenerate exported tables and figures. Location-direction labels now describe parameter differences rather than asserting that entire subgroup response curves are harder or easier.

Recompute older estimate_bias() / estimate_all_bias() results from the saved fit and matching diagnostics to obtain boundary and complete-cell information/fit checks. Search-boundary estimates remain points, with unavailable SEs and screening tail areas. Small positive response variances contribute to information; missing residuals no longer produce partial-cell Infit/Outfit. Facet labels containing || now identify distinct cells correctly. The summary reports missing screening counts and retains unavailable cells in Bonferroni/Holm family sizes. These changes require re-screening, not refitting the calibration; an old saved table is not recalculated by plotting or printing it.

Results from estimate_bias(), estimate_all_bias(), unexpected_response_table(), unexpected_after_bias_table() and displacement_table() now carry a fit_identity field. When a consumer combines a supplied result with a fit, it checks that they describe the same analysis. This includes reports, dashboards, QC, export/replay helpers and build_misfit_casebook(). Every retained member and the primary result of a bias collection must match. Matching facet labels alone is insufficient.

Older results without this metadata, and manually assembled bias tables, cannot establish that match. Recreate the result from its saved fit and matching diagnostics; do not add an identity field to an old table by hand. Use the original facets, estimation limits, filtering rules and thresholds. For example, if the original bias screen used these options:


bias <- estimate_bias(fit, diagnostics,
  facet_a = "Rater", facet_b = "Criterion",
  max_abs = 10, omit_extreme = TRUE, max_iter = 2, tol = 1e-3)
saveRDS(bias, "bias-0.2.4.rds")
report <- build_apa_outputs(fit, diagnostics, bias_results = bias)

The same calls and table columns remain available; the added metadata is stored alongside the tables. Recomputing the screen does not refit the model. Standalone summary/plot methods keep their existing input requirements and do not establish a relationship to a separately supplied fit. These identity checks prevent accidental mixing; they do not validate manually edited numbers or make a screening result eligible for formal inference.

Updating saved predictions in 0.2.4

predict_mfrm_units() and sample_mfrm_plausible_values() now retain a fit_identity field. Fit-level manifests, replay scripts and archive exports require that identity to match the supplied calibration, fitted population coding and source scoring status. Recreate older outputs from the saved fit and original scoring inputs, retaining the original column mappings, person_data, prior, integration settings, omission policy and seed. This repeats scoring or drawing plausible values, not estimation of the calibration model. Standalone summary/plot methods retain their existing input rules; a standalone table does not establish a match to another fit.

predict_mfrm_population() is a simulation-based design forecast. A result created with fit = fit must match that source fit when attached to an archive. Recreating an older fit-derived forecast repeats its simulations and replication fits; the original calibration fit can be reused. A result created with sim_spec = spec remains an explicitly supplied scenario and can accompany a different fit. Its notes and the manifest's population_prediction_source setting distinguish this from a forecast derived from the attached fit. Do not change the source label of an old result to bypass the check.

Generated replay scripts continue to use the saved simulation specification. They reproduce those forecasting assumptions rather than deriving new ones from the replayed calibration, which could change the forecast. The recreated forecast is therefore labelled as a supplied-specification scenario. Identity checks do not change scoring uncertainty, eligibility or the interpretation of plausible values and Monte Carlo forecast uncertainty.

Updating saved structural reviews in 0.2.4

analyze_hierarchical_structure() now saves data_identity metadata. reporting_checklist() checks the reviewed column roles and retained rows, including scores when ICC was computed. Raw-data reviews and reviews of a subset of fitted facets remain supported when those data match; the checklist names their scope. Row order, factor level order, unused columns and fitted estimates are irrelevant to this descriptive-data match. Different rating counts, assignments or ICC scores are not interchangeable.

Recreate an older review from its saved fit or matching retained rows using the original facets, person/score columns, ICC and connectivity options, missing-value policy and interval settings (including bootstrap seed). This repeats the requested structural/ICC review, not MFRM estimation. Do not add identity metadata to old tables manually. Standalone summary and plot methods retain their existing requirements. Reviews of additional raw rows or grouping columns absent from the fit must be reported separately; they cannot mark this fit's structural-review checklist item as available. Recalculate nesting reviews involving fractional/zero weights or missing facet values: detect_facet_nesting() now uses weighted frequencies directly and one common set of observed rows per pair. Earlier results rounded weights and mixed marginal and conditional samples. Weight columns must now be numeric, finite and nonnegative, with some positive weight; missing columns and invalid values are refused instead of ignored or replaced. New UsedRows/ExcludedRows columns record the pair-specific scope.

Rating-count review corrections in 0.2.4

In facet_small_sample_review(), facet_summary$WorstCategory now selects the lowest count band, correcting the previous highest-band aggregation. Recreate the review from the saved fit to update older review objects. Count thresholds must now be finite, positive and strictly increasing. The table columns and default thresholds remain the same; the returned notes field explains that counts are retained rating rows and cannot establish precision or coverage.

In reporting_checklist(), the item formerly named "Facet sample-size adequacy" is now "Facet rating-count screening". Scripts selecting that item by its text must use the new label. Its availability indicates that a count screen is present, including sparse counts, rather than treating a high count band as proof of sample adequacy.

Retained table-field names

  • row_review is the data-quality table field used to document row filtering. FACETS-style column and metric contract results are exposed as column_review and metric_checks.

  • Prediction outputs expose row-preparation and person-omission traceability as row_review and population_review.

  • hierarchical_review, shrinkage_review, and nesting_review are manifest or model-comparison traceability fields. They are not callable helper names; user-facing helper names use review/check terminology.

Typical workflow

  • Legacy handoff: run_mfrm_facets() -> build_fixed_reports() -> facets_output_file_bundle() plus write_mfrm_residual_file() / write_mfrm_subset_file() only when those standalone files are needed.

  • Mixed workflow: RSM / PCM: fit_mfrm() -> diagnose_mfrm() -> build_apa_outputs() -> compatibility export only if required. GPCM: fit_mfrm() -> diagnose_mfrm() -> reporting_checklist() -> facets_output_file_bundle() only when a graph/score handoff is needed, retaining its package-native GPCM caveats.

  • FACETS output-contract review: fit_mfrm() -> diagnose_mfrm() -> facets_output_contract_review().

Companion guides

  • For FACETS coverage and boundary wording, see facets_positioning_guide() and facets_feature_coverage().

  • For standard reports/tables, see mfrmr_reports_and_tables.

  • For manuscript-draft reporting, see mfrmr_reporting_and_apa.

  • For visual diagnostics, see mfrmr_visual_diagnostics.

  • For linking and DFF workflows, see mfrmr_linking_and_dff.

  • For end-to-end routes, see mfrmr_workflow_methods.

Examples

toy <- load_mfrmr_data("example_core")
toy_small <- toy[toy$Person %in% unique(toy$Person)[1:12], , drop = FALSE]

run <- run_mfrm_facets(
  data = toy_small,
  person = "Person",
  facets = c("Rater", "Criterion"),
  score = "Score",
  maxit = 30
)
summary(run)
#> FACETS-style Workflow Summary
#>   Model: RSM | Method: JML
#>   N: 192 | Persons: 12 | Facets: 2 | Categories: 4
#>   LogLik: -203.282 | Information-criterion ranking is unavailable for JML.
#>   Optimizer returned code 0: Yes | Formal inference: Ready | Iterations: 66
#> 
#> Column mapping
#>     Key            Value
#>  Person           Person
#>   Score            Score
#>  Facets Rater, Criterion
#>  Weight                 
#> 
#> Detailed objects:
#>  - summary(out$fit)
#>  - summary(out$diagnostics)
compatibility_alias_table("functions")
#>                       Alias           PreferredName  Surface      Lifecycle
#> 1               mfrmRFacets         run_mfrm_facets function retained_alias
#> 2               analyze_dif             analyze_dff function retained_alias
#> 3              mfrm_cluster        mfrm_cluster_pam function retained_alias
#> 4 mfrm_response_imputations review_mfrm_imputations function retained_alias
#>                                                   RetainedFor
#> 1                                      older workflow scripts
#> 2                           earlier DIF-oriented package code
#> 3        earlier feature-clustering scripts and saved results
#> 4 earlier assigned-score imputation scripts and saved results
#>             RemovalPlan
#> 1 No scheduled removal.
#> 2 No scheduled removal.
#> 3 No scheduled removal.
#> 4 No scheduled removal.
#>                                                                                                   Notes
#> 1                                    Compatibility wrapper for the legacy-compatible one-shot workflow.
#> 2               DFF naming is preferred for many-facet workflows; the older DIF name is still accepted.
#> 3 Identical Gower/PAM implementation and result class; the preferred name makes the algorithm explicit.
#> 4        Same supplied-completion checks and result class; this function does not generate imputations.

fixed <- build_fixed_reports(
  estimate_bias(
    run$fit,
    run$diagnostics,
    facet_a = "Rater",
    facet_b = "Criterion",
    max_iter = 1
  ),
  branch = "original"
)
names(fixed)
#> [1] "bias_fixed"        "pairwise_fixed"    "pairwise_table"   
#> [4] "branch"            "style"             "interaction_label"
#> [7] "target_facet"
